workarounds.note: createBundle in 1.4.1 has no localized input, so each edition writes a single-locale bundle of its own from the same config factory and LANG; openBundle already reads bilingual files such as postext.dev/bundles/postext-guide.postext

readBundle localises the base resource types to the locale the reader asks for, not the one it serves, so the Spanish file opened with { locale: 'en' } (and imported at /en/sandbox, whose parseBundle passes the interface language) prints Figure 1.1 while bundle.locale says 'es'; the config writes resourceTypes: defaultResourceTypes(LANG) into the file, which replaces the base key

a heading design kept in the column is cut at the text block's top and bottom edges (not at its sides), so the cover heading is span: 'page' in a one-column leaflet; without it the art starts 12 mm down, stops 13 mm above the bottom edge and the language tab shrinks to a strip without its letters

an inline ('here') resource gets space above it but none below: the paragraph after the hours table started 1.4 mm under its caption, against 4.7 mm above the table; :::space{lines=0.5} after the embed gives 3.7 mm
the H1 breakBefore is restated because a headings object drops it; the cover opens the leaflet, so it changes nothing on these pages
hyphenation matches the exact code, so the English edition says 'en-us'; the same value sets the PDF's /Lang (en-US and es in the two files)
the palette does not reach design-slot colours (the cover's kicker, title, lead, facts and tab, the foot strip); col() writes the hex beside every paletteId

renderToPdf embeds one font program per requested face key, so each PDF carries 10 font programs for the 7 faces its pages use (DM Sans Italic and Instrument Sans 400 and 700 twice, 40-43 KB in all); a pen cannot route around it, noted so the file size is not taken for a recipe fault
design text lineHeight is a multiple of the size (0.96 for the cover title, 1.4 for the lead), never a pt() value
